summary: Chökyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Young Lamas Home School and Rumtek Monastery (~1964–1974) under teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery in 1976 and founded Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Chönyi Drolma studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, Yü studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973). She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University, serving as Professor (~2001–2013) and later Sheng Yen Professor Emerita (~2013).

Kidwell studied at the University of Oklahoma (master's ~1963–1966, Ph.D. ~1966–1970). Her posts included UC Berkeley (~1980–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), the University of Oklahoma (from 1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (director ~2007–2011).

A philosopher and religious studies scholar, Carlisle studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London (~2020).

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at the École Normale Supérieure, ENLOV, and Paris Descartes University under André Martinet. His posts included CNRS (~1965–1970), the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE (~1970–1988), and the Collège de France (1988–2006).

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Jacques studied under George Cœdès (~1960–1969). He taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1998) and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1989–1992).

Lévi-Strauss studied at the Paris Law Faculty (~1927–1931) under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1951–1974), EHESS (~1975–1982), and Collège de France as chair of Anthropologie sociale (1959–1982).
Benthien studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2005).
Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Weber studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Buchanan, active in Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Glasgow (1782) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he was appointed Vice-Provost of Fort William College.

Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD (~1970–1973) and Habilitation (~1977–1983) at the University of Hamburg. He served as Dozent at Hamburg (~1983–1989) and head of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Specializing in Indology and Tibetology, Vogel earned his PhD and completed his habilitation at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau. He taught at Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Bonn (Ordinarius 1976–1998).
Montelle is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who held posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.
Linguist Clemente Merlo studied at the University of Pavia (~1898–1903) and held a post at the University of Pisa (~1911–1953).
Seely is an Indology scholar affiliated with the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).
Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

An Indology and linguistics scholar, Caillat studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS, the University of Lyon, Sorbonne University (1967–1988), Collège de France (Director ~1987–1999), and Institut de France (~1987–2007).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Sciberras studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David Edward Cooper and Simon P. James, as well as traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
